articles.title: I built a QR code phishing scanner for our free API — and ended up writing a PNG decoder from scratch to make it work.
articles.excerpt: ** ** The problem QR code phishing ("quishing") is one of the fastest-growing phishing vectors right now — Microsoft's 2026 report puts the year-over-year growth at 146% in Q1 alone, and QR codes now…
articles.body: ** ** The problem QR code phishing ("quishing") is one of the fastest-growing phishing vectors right now — Microsoft's 2026 report puts the year-over-year growth at 146% in Q1 alone, and QR codes now account for roughly 12% of all phishing attacks, up from under 1% in 2021. The attack specifically slips past text-based email filters, since the malicious URL is hidden inside an image. I wanted to add an endpoint to Presend's API that decodes a QR code from an uploaded image and, if it points to a URL, checks that URL against a malware/phishing database — decode plus reputation check in one call. The API runs on Cloudflare Workers, which meant no Canvas, no Node's Buffer, no filesystem, and a strict script-size budget.
articles.author: Presendapp

articles.title: Carrying two phones is hard, but iOS 27 has a solution Android ought to copy
articles.excerpt: Apple will allow two iPhones to share a single phone number, and Android should copy this to streamline multi-device setups.
articles.body: Credit: Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority TL;DR Apple is introducing “iPhone Handoff” in iOS 27, allowing a single cellular plan and phone number to be shared between a primary iPhone and a secondary companion iPhone via dual eSIMs. Unlike basic Continuity features that require Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, iPhone Handoff could potentially operate natively at the network level, keeping the companion device fully connected even when the main phone is switched off. Android has no such feature in the works for network-level phone number sharing, and it needs to copy this to reduce multi-device friction across Android’s varied form factors and use cases, such as foldables, camera phones, gaming handhelds, tablets, and even laptops.
articles.author: Aamir Siddiqui

articles.title: Context Engineering: o ativo que a maioria ainda trata como prompt
articles.excerpt: Em 2026, a maior parte das discussões sobre agentes de código ainda gira em torno do modelo: qual é o melhor, qual tem a janela de contexto maior, qual gera código mais rápido. Há, no entanto, um cons…
articles.body: Em 2026, a maior parte das discussões sobre agentes de código ainda gira em torno do modelo: qual é o melhor, qual tem a janela de contexto maior, qual gera código mais rápido. Há, no entanto, um consenso crescente na literatura e na prática de engenharia: o gargalo principal deixou de ser a capacidade de geração. Passou a ser o contexto. Context Engineering é a disciplina de decidir, de forma deliberada, o que o agente vê em cada momento e o que ele não vê. Não se trata apenas de escrever um prompt melhor. Trata-se de projetar a informação que entra na janela de contexto, o que permanece entre sessões e o que é recuperado sob demanda. 🔍 Por que contexto se tornou o ponto crítico? Agentes de código operam com uma janela de contexto finita.
articles.author: Alex Pimenta

articles.title: Laravel Cloud vs Forge vs a Self-Hosted VPS
articles.excerpt: Laravel Cloud vs Forge vs a Self-Hosted VPS Three paths exist for getting a Laravel application into production: let Laravel Cloud handle everything, use Forge to manage your own servers, or configure…
articles.body: Laravel Cloud vs Forge vs a Self-Hosted VPS Three paths exist for getting a Laravel application into production: let Laravel Cloud handle everything, use Forge to manage your own servers, or configure a VPS from scratch. Each represents a different point on the control-vs-convenience spectrum, and picking the wrong one costs you either money, engineering time, or both. This article cuts straight to the trade-offs. It assumes you already understand basic Laravel deployment concepts — if you want the broader picture, the Laravel Deployment and Hosting: Cloud, Forge, VPS, Docker, and Octane guide covers the full stack. Prerequisites: Laravel 12 (PHP 8.2+) or Laravel 13 (PHP 8.3+), Composer 2.x, a GitHub/GitLab repository. For Forge: an account at forge.laravel.com.

articles.title: Poll shows Amazon’s Kindle DRM crackdown is backfiring with loyal ebook fans
articles.excerpt: Are Amazon's decisions killing the Kindle?
articles.body: It’s safe to suggest that the Amazon Kindle range is the industry’s leading e-reader. Even for those who aren’t too familiar with its maker, the Kindle name is often used as a blanket term for all digital book readers. This perhaps gave Amazon a sense of security in the market, but given its recent decisions, this dominance could come toppling down sooner rather than later. At the end of August, Amazon rolled out an update to the Kindle Oasis that closed a Libby loophole that allowed extended borrowing. More importantly, it also strengthened the platform’s DRM, making it even tougher for users to back up their books to other devices. For some users, like my colleague Dhruv , this is the last straw.
articles.author: Andy Walker

articles.title: A small privacy decision that changed my web calculator
articles.excerpt: I built Calculator Toolkit for a narrow moment: someone has a restaurant bill, wants to check the tip and tax math, then needs to split the total with a few people. At first I treated the no-account r…
articles.body: I built Calculator Toolkit for a narrow moment: someone has a restaurant bill, wants to check the tip and tax math, then needs to split the total with a few people. At first I treated the no-account requirement as a small feature. It turned out to be the decision that shaped most of the interface. A saved-history feature would be convenient. It would also mean sign-in, account recovery, data retention, and an extra decision for someone who only wants to settle a dinner bill. I decided that the calculator should run locally in the browser instead. There is no account and no bill-data upload. That creates constraints. A person cannot return tomorrow and recover an earlier calculation. There is no dashboard where an unclear result can be explained later.
articles.author: Leon

articles.body: Hay un malentendido fundamental sobre las apuestas deportivas: la gente cree que se trata de acertar quién gana. No es así. Se trata de encontrar situaciones en las que la cuota del mercado está equivocada respecto a la probabilidad real. Eso es el value betting , y es matemáticamente idéntico a buscar activos infravalorados en bolsa. El problema Necesitaba dos cosas: (1) una estimación propia y fiable de la probabilidad de cada resultado, y (2) una forma de compararla con las cuotas del mercado para detectar valor y dimensionar la apuesta sin arruinarme. La probabilidad: reutilizar el Sports Engine Las probabilidades vienen del modelo del Sports Performance Engine (ensemble LightGBM + XGBoost sobre datos StatsBomb).

articles.title: A Technical Review Template for AI Support Changes
articles.excerpt: Support automation is an operational system. It needs maintained inputs, observable decisions, test cases, owners, and a safe path back to a human team. This article applies that discipline to change…
articles.body: Support automation is an operational system. It needs maintained inputs, observable decisions, test cases, owners, and a safe path back to a human team. This article applies that discipline to change review . The practical goal is: Review scope, sources, expected behavior, boundary cases, tests, owner, and rollback. The same method is useful whether the first implementation is a spreadsheet, an internal tool, or an AI-assisted support product. Define the support contract first Start by turning change review into a contract that a merchant, support lead, and developer can all inspect. Name the customer question being handled, the facts required to answer it, the conditions that modify the answer, and the point where information alone is not enough.

articles.title: Building an E-Commerce Web Data Pipeline That Does Not Lie to You
articles.excerpt: You scrape a competitor product page, load the price into a dashboard, and everything looks fine. Then someone asks why the alert fired at 3 a.m. for a “70% price drop” that never happened. The page c…
articles.body: You scrape a competitor product page, load the price into a dashboard, and everything looks fine. Then someone asks why the alert fired at 3 a.m. for a “70% price drop” that never happened. The page changed currency based on location, your parser grabbed the crossed-out price, and the pipeline treated bad data as a market signal. Public web data is useful in e-commerce, but the hard part is not just collecting it. The hard part is making sure it means what you think it means.

articles.title: Rocket issues delay 1st-ever private mission to Venus: 'We are awaiting Neutron readiness'
articles.excerpt: The first-ever private mission to Venus is still groundbound due to delays with its launch vehicle, Rocket Lab's Neutron. But team members remain bullish on the groundbreaking mission.
articles.body: The future of a privately backed robotic mission Venus seems about as cloudy as the planet itself at the moment. Scientists based at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) are working with the California-based company Rocket Lab to search for possible signs of life on Venus. The first step in that program is the Rocket Lab Mission to Venus , which will deploy a small, nose cone-like probe crafted to sample the Venusian atmosphere using a device called an autofluorescence nephelometer (AFN). That AFN can measure individual particles in Venusian clouds , constraining their size, shape and composition in a search for signs of organic molecules.But that undertaking, primarily fueled by private dollars, has been waylaid due to getting a needed booster flight-qualified.

articles.title: I’m slowly escaping Google’s ecosystem, and it’s easier than I thought
articles.excerpt: A lot of Google services have been surprisingly easy to live without.
articles.body: Google’s got products to fill almost every consumer tech niche, from web search to smartphones to connected cameras to office software. For a long time, I liked that about the company; using Google’s services everywhere I could felt like a way to simplify my technological life. I’ve gotten a lot of value out of Google’s big, interconnected ecosystem over the years. But as the company’s put its weight behind converting Search into a chatbot and adding Gemini-powered features I don’t use to every corner of every app and device, I’ve found myself wishing I wasn’t so invested in its products . I’ve stuck around mostly because of inertia: I’m used to Google, and it’s already got all my data, and moving to competing services seemed like a big undertaking.

articles.title: Astronomers discover mysterious 10-sided cloud structure at Saturn's south pole
articles.excerpt: A mysterious giant 10-sided pattern of clouds has recently formed around Saturn's south pole, a new study finds.
articles.body: A mysterious giant 10-sided pattern of clouds has recently formed around Saturn's south pole, a new study finds. This newfound "decagon" joins the bizarre colossal hexagon seen for decades at Saturn's north pole. Saturn's hexagon — a cloud pattern about 20,000 miles (32,000 kilometers) wide — was first discovered in 1988 by scientists reviewing data from NASA's Voyager flybys of Saturn in 1980 and 1981. Despite decades of observations, no similar structure was seen anywhere else on Saturn — until now, as scientists have discovered an even larger structure on Saturn . The newfound decagon is about 104,250 miles (167,820 kilometers) wide, with each of its 10 sides measuring about 10,425 miles (16,782 km) long.

articles.title: I rented a car, and within hours, my driver's license was for sale
articles.excerpt: The FBI is reportedly investigating a massive data breach that is unfolding in real time.
articles.body: Not long ago, I rented an SUV from a well-known car rental company. Within hours of an employee scanning my driver's license, a high-resolution scan of my ID was available for sale on the dark web. An exposé published Tuesday by KrebsOnSecurity reports that my license was one of more than 153 million that were available through Nexus, the name of the new ID theft service. Like other driver's licenses available there—including some belonging to journalist Brian Krebs, his mother, an FBI assistant director, and several security researchers—my license was purported to include multiple image files showing both the front and back of the ID. Besides a basic image scan, the files also captured the images in the infrared and ultraviolet spectrums.

Honestly, this is probably where the $166 million "The Mandalorian" spinoff movie should have premiered in the first place, but Disney decided to test the big screen waters with its charismatic clansman and Baby Yoda. Sadly, it came up a bit short when all the tickets were tallied, but everyone loves second chances, and we're pretty psyched to see the space fantasy back where it belongs: in the vast streaming universe.
